description: Establish a green baseline on a new branch before making changes. Confirm the backend and frontend build and their existing tests pass, and record the coverage baseline so later changes can be measured against a known-good state.
steps: From /projects/sandbox/pantry, create and check out a new branch off master named `fix-scans-not-appearing` (do NOT push).
Confirm the Go toolchain: run `go version` (expect go1.26.0). If a `compile: version does not match go tool version` or GOROOT/GOTOOLCHAIN mismatch appears, run `mise install go@1.26.0` and retry.
Run backend tests scoped to exclude the stray vendored package under node_modules: `go test $(go list ./... | grep -v node_modules)`. Confirm green.

Run the coverage gate from repo root: `./scripts/test-coverage.sh`. Note the reported total coverage and current COVERAGE_THRESHOLD. If the raw `go test ./...` inside it fails ONLY due to a package under frontend/node_modules, record that as a known sandbox artifact (do not treat as a real failure) and capture the coverage number the backend packages produce.
Run frontend checks from /projects/sandbox/pantry/frontend: `npx tsc -b`, then `npm run lint`, then `npx vitest --run`. Confirm all green.
Record the baseline results (build ok, backend tests pass/fail, frontend checks pass/fail, coverage %) in this feature's findings field.
acceptance_criteria: A new branch `fix-scans-not-appearing` exists and is checked out (git branch --show-current prints it).
Frontend `npx tsc -b`, `npm run lint`, and `npx vitest --run` all pass.
The coverage baseline (total % and threshold) is recorded in findings, along with whether the node_modules sweep artifact was observed.
verification: go test $(go list ./... | grep -v node_modules) exits 0
cd frontend && npx tsc -b && npm run lint && npx vitest --run all exit 0
findings:
Baseline established on branch fix-scans-not-appearing (created off master at afb1abb). No code changes made in this feature.

Toolchain: `go version` -> go1.26.0 linux/amd64 (no mismatch on the host `go`; no `mise install go@1.26.0` needed for the direct go commands).

Backend tests (scoped, mirrors CI): `go test $(go list ./... | grep -v node_modules)` PASSED - all 11 packages ok (cmd/server, internal/app, internal/events, internal/inventory, internal/product, internal/scan, internal/scanlistener, internal/server, internal/shopping, internal/suggestion, internal/webui). internal/events is slow (~26-29s) but green.

Coverage: current COVERAGE_THRESHOLD in scripts/test-coverage.sh is 74.9%. Running ./scripts/test-coverage.sh UNSCOPED exits 1 - CONFIRMED sandbox artifact: the unscoped `go test ./...` sweeps a stray vendored Go standard-library/toolchain copy under frontend/node_modules that was built with go1.25.1, producing many `compile: version "go1.26.0" does not match go tool version "go1.25.1"` errors and tripping `set -e` before the total is printed. Real CI has no node_modules in the Go job. Also note: on abort, the script's cleanup `rm -f coverage.out` does not run, so it leaves a stray coverage.out (removed manually; it is git-ignored/untracked, not a source change). Threshold line in the script was NOT modified (script aborted before the self-update step).

To get an accurate baseline coverage number matching CI, ran coverage scoped to the same non-node_modules packages: `go test -cover -coverpkg=<scoped pkgs> -coverprofile ...` -> TOTAL 75.2% of statements (above the 74.9% threshold). This is the real backend coverage baseline.

Frontend (from /projects/sandbox/pantry/frontend): node/npm were NOT on PATH; installed via `mise install node@24` (needed MISE_NODE_VERIFY=false MISE_NODE_GPG_VERIFY=false because gpg-agent is unavailable in the sandbox and blocks signature verification; the tarball itself downloads fine). node v24.21.0 / npm 11.19.0. Run frontend commands with `mise exec node@24 -- <cmd>`.
  - `npx tsc -b` PASSED (exit 0).
  - `npm run lint` (eslint .) PASSED (exit 0).
  - `npx vitest --run` PASSED: 20 test files, 147 tests passed.

Summary: build ok; backend tests pass; frontend tsc/lint/vitest all pass; coverage baseline 75.2% total vs 74.9% threshold; node_modules coverage-sweep artifact WAS observed (use the scoped go list command for backend runs; use `mise exec node@24 --` for frontend).
